title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - B-4
notes:
South needs trumps to be 3-2 to have a chance to make the contract. The general plan must be to set up the clubs by ruffing South's club losers in the dummy.

South has a line of play available that will ensure the contract any time clubs are no worse than 4-2, assuming spades break 3-2. South should win the opening trump lead and draw a second round of trump.

To guard against a 4-2 club break South must leave the master trump outstanding and begin to play on clubs. South plays a club to the ♣K and returns to the ♣A. South ruffs a club in the dummy. When clubs prove to be 4-2, South crosses back to his hand and takes another club ruff in the dummy.

South's last club is now high. The defense will eventually get a trump trick as the only defensive winner.
